title: Normalization of a unital coherent cocone of categories
statement:
Let $I$ be a small directed partially ordered set, let $(\mathcal C_i)_{i\in I}$ be categories, and let $\mathcal D$ be a category, in fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Give functors $T_{ij}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ for $i\le j$, functors $\Phi_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D$, and natural isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}:\Phi_jT_{ij}\cong\Phi_i$, that is, a category cocone [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-cocone]. Also give natural isomorphisms $\epsilon_i:T_{ii}\cong\mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal C_i}$ and $\tau_{ijk}:T_{jk}T_{ij}\cong T_{ik}$. Assume the pentagon
$$\tau_{ikl}\circ(T_{kl}\tau_{ijk})=\tau_{ijl}\circ(\tau_{jkl}T_{ij})$$
for $i\le j\le k\le l$, the unit identities $\tau_{iij}=T_{ij}\epsilon_i$ and $\tau_{ijj}=\epsilon_jT_{ij}$, and the cocone identities
$$\theta_{ik}\circ\Phi_k(\tau_{ijk})=\theta_{ij}\circ(\theta_{jk}T_{ij}),\qquad \theta_{ii}=\Phi_i(\epsilon_i).$$
Functor associators and unitors are understood in these equations. There exists a cocone with the same $\mathcal C_i,\mathcal D,\Phi_i$ and transitions $T'_{ij}$, together with natural isomorphisms $\beta_{ij}:T'_{ij}\cong T_{ij}$, such that $T'_{ii}=\mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal C_i}$, $\beta_{ii}=\epsilon_i^{-1}$, and, when $i\ne j$, $T'_{ij}=T_{ij}$ and $\beta_{ij}=\mathrm{id}$. Its comparisons are
$$\theta'_{ij}=\theta_{ij}\circ\Phi_j(\beta_{ij}),\qquad
\tau'_{ijk}=\beta_{ik}^{-1}\circ\tau_{ijk}\circ(T_{jk}\beta_{ij})\circ(\beta_{jk}T'_{ij}).$$
These comparisons satisfy the coherence and strict normalization hypotheses of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-model]; in particular $\theta'_{ii}$, $\tau'_{iij}$ and $\tau'_{ijj}$ are identities. The original cocone satisfies each of (Obj), (Hom-surj), (Hom-inj) of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions] if and only if the normalized cocone does, respectively. Under the displayed $\beta$ identifications, a finite-stage arrow $g:T_{ik}x\to T_{jk}y$ corresponds to $\beta_{jk,y}^{-1}\circ g\circ\beta_{ik,x}$, and its image $\theta_{jk,y}\circ\Phi_k(g)\circ\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}$ in $\mathcal D$ is unchanged.

source.place: Statement, normalization and compatibility hypotheses; auxiliary normalization lemma supplying these hypotheses for the unital tensor cocone (agent formulation, no assertion that this lemma is already proved in the source)

proof.text: For each comparable pair define $T'_{ij}=\mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal C_i}$ if $i=j$ and $T'_{ij}=T_{ij}$ otherwise, and define $\beta_{ii}=\epsilon_i^{-1}$ and $\beta_{ij}=\mathrm{id}$ otherwise. Equal-index cases are read after substituting $j=i$. These are functors and natural isomorphisms in the original universes. Keep $\Phi_i$ and $\mathcal D$ and put $\theta'_{ij}=\theta_{ij}\circ\Phi_j(\beta_{ij})$. This gives exactly the transition, vertex-functor and natural-isomorphism data of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-cocone].

source.place: Statement, cocone data and normalization; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
Write products of morphisms or natural transformations in right-to-left order, suppressing functor associators and unitors as in the statement. Define
$$B_{ijk}=(T_{jk}\beta_{ij})(\beta_{jk}T'_{ij}):T'_{jk}T'_{ij}\longrightarrow T_{jk}T_{ij},\qquad \tau'_{ijk}=\beta_{ik}^{-1}\tau_{ijk}B_{ijk}.$$
Whiskering a natural isomorphism gives a natural isomorphism: for example, its naturality square is the image under the whiskering functor of the original square, or that square evaluated on the image of a morphism. Composition and inversion preserve naturality by composing squares and cancelling invertible components. Hence these formulas give natural isomorphisms of the required types, and
$$\beta_{ik}\tau'_{ijk}=\tau_{ijk}B_{ijk}.$$
This equality will be used componentwise in the following calculations.

source.place: Statement, cocycle and compatibility: definition of the transported comparisons; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
Fix $i\le j\le k\le l$ and set
$$B_{ijkl}=(T_{kl}T_{jk}\beta_{ij})(T_{kl}\beta_{jk}T'_{ij})(\beta_{kl}T'_{jk}T'_{ij}).$$
Expand the left side of the desired pentagon and use naturality of $\beta_{kl}$ on $\tau'_{ijk}$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{il}\tau'_{ikl}(T'_{kl}\tau'_{ijk})
&=\tau_{ikl}(T_{kl}\beta_{ik})(\beta_{kl}T'_{ik})(T'_{kl}\tau'_{ijk})\\
&=\tau_{ikl}T_{kl}(\beta_{ik}\tau'_{ijk})(\beta_{kl}T'_{jk}T'_{ij})\\
&=\tau_{ikl}(T_{kl}\tau_{ijk})B_{ijkl}.
\end{aligned}$$
All expressions are natural transformations from $T'_{kl}T'_{jk}T'_{ij}$ to $T_{il}$, so the substitutions are typed even when indices coincide.

source.place: Statement, cocycle: first pentagon composite; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
For the other pentagon composite, the same definitions and naturality of $\tau_{jkl}$ on $\beta_{ij}$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{il}\tau'_{ijl}(\tau'_{jkl}T'_{ij})
&=\tau_{ijl}(T_{jl}\beta_{ij})\bigl((\beta_{jl}\tau'_{jkl})T'_{ij}\bigr)\\
&=\tau_{ijl}(T_{jl}\beta_{ij})(\tau_{jkl}T'_{ij})(B_{jkl}T'_{ij})\\
&=\tau_{ijl}(\tau_{jkl}T_{ij})B_{ijkl}.
\end{aligned}$$
The original pentagon equates the final expressions of this step and step 3. Cancel the invertible $\beta_{il}$ to obtain $\tau'_{ikl}(T'_{kl}\tau'_{ijk})=\tau'_{ijl}(\tau'_{jkl}T'_{ij})$. This uses only the given pentagon and the displayed naturality square, including repeated-index cases.

source.place: Statement, cocycle: second composite and cancellation; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
Since $T'_{ii}=\mathrm{Id}$, the first unit identity and the formula for $\tau'$ give
$$\tau'_{iij}=\beta_{ij}^{-1}(T_{ij}\epsilon_i)(T_{ij}\epsilon_i^{-1})\beta_{ij}=\mathrm{id}.$$
This calculation also covers $i=j$: the factor $\beta_{ij}T'_{ii}$ is just $\beta_{ij}$ after removing the identity functor, so no separate assumption about $\epsilon_i$ is used.

source.place: Statement, normalization: first repeated-index comparison; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
For the second unit identity use naturality of $\epsilon_j:T_{jj}\cong\mathrm{Id}$ on $\beta_{ij}$:
$$(\epsilon_jT_{ij})(T_{jj}\beta_{ij})=\beta_{ij}(\epsilon_jT'_{ij}).$$
Substitute this into the defining formula, using $\beta_{jj}=\epsilon_j^{-1}$:
$$\tau'_{ijj}=\beta_{ij}^{-1}(\epsilon_jT_{ij})(T_{jj}\beta_{ij})(\epsilon_j^{-1}T'_{ij})=\mathrm{id}.$$
The same equality applies when $i=j$ and proves the second unit clause also in the fully diagonal case.

source.place: Statement, normalization: second repeated-index comparison; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
Naturality of $\theta_{jk}:\Phi_kT_{jk}\cong\Phi_j$ on $\beta_{ij}$ and the original cocone identity give
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta'_{ik}\Phi_k(\tau'_{ijk})
&=\theta_{ik}\Phi_k(\tau_{ijk}B_{ijk})\\
&=\theta_{ij}(\theta_{jk}T_{ij})\Phi_k(T_{jk}\beta_{ij})\Phi_k(\beta_{jk}T'_{ij})\\
&=\theta_{ij}\Phi_j(\beta_{ij})(\theta_{jk}T'_{ij})\Phi_k(\beta_{jk}T'_{ij})\\
&=\theta'_{ij}(\theta'_{jk}T'_{ij}).
\end{aligned}$$
Also $\theta'_{ii}=\Phi_i(\epsilon_i)\Phi_i(\epsilon_i^{-1})=\mathrm{id}$. Thus steps 3--6 and this step verify precisely the normalization, cocycle and compatibility hypotheses stated in [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-model]. Here compatibility can equivalently be written by composing on the right with $\Phi_k(\tau'_{ijk})^{-1}$; we do not invoke any theorem about the colimit category.

source.place: Statement, normalization, cocycle and compatibility; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
For $k\ge i,j$, $x\in\mathcal C_i$ and $y\in\mathcal C_j$, write $b_x=\beta_{ik,x}$ and $b_y=\beta_{jk,y}$. The map
$$g\longmapsto\widehat g=b_y^{-1}gb_x$$
is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(T_{ik}x,T_{jk}y)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(T'_{ik}x,T'_{jk}y)$, with inverse $h\mapsto b_yhb_x^{-1}$; the two composites are identities by cancellation. Its image in $\mathcal D$ is unchanged, since
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta'_{jk,y}\Phi_k(\widehat g)(\theta'_{ik,x})^{-1}
&=\theta_{jk,y}\Phi_k(b_y)\Phi_k(b_y^{-1}gb_x)\Phi_k(b_x)^{-1}\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}\\
&=\theta_{jk,y}\Phi_k(g)\theta_{ik,x}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the stated arrow correspondence, in both directions and also when $k=i$ or $k=j$.

source.place: Statement, comparison-functor formula: preservation of finite-stage images; explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text: The condition (Obj) of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions] involves only $\mathcal D$ and the $\Phi_i$, which were kept exactly, so its witnesses agree. For (Hom-surj), keep the indices $i,j,k$, the objects $x,y$, and the morphism $\varphi$. Replace a witness $g$ by $\widehat g$ from step 8. The image equality there proves that it is a witness for the normalized condition. Conversely replace a normalized witness $h$ by $b_yhb_x^{-1}$ and use the same equality. Thus (Hom-surj) holds for one cocone exactly when it holds for the other.

source.place: Filtered 2-colimit conditions, (Obj) and (Hom-surj); explicit agent calculation, not a proof asserted by the source

proof.text:
For (Hom-inj) of [det-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit-conditions], its quantified morphisms $g,g':x\to y$ at stage $k$ and its premise $\Phi_k(g)=\Phi_k(g')$ are unchanged. At every possible witness $l\ge k$, naturality of $\beta_{kl}$ gives
$$T_{kl}(g)=\beta_{kl,y}T'_{kl}(g)\beta_{kl,x}^{-1},\qquad T_{kl}(g')=\beta_{kl,y}T'_{kl}(g')\beta_{kl,x}^{-1}.$$
Cancelling the same isomorphisms shows $T_{kl}(g)=T_{kl}(g')$ if and only if $T'_{kl}(g)=T'_{kl}(g')$. Consequently exactly the same witness indices work in the two versions, proving (Hom-inj) in both directions and completing every clause.
